The offline test set has **11.8K query-level instances involving 93K unique member profiles** (page 6, Section 5.1).

Each instance has one clicked candidate as the positive and three negatives. The negatives come from non-clicked impressions and randomly sampled members (page 6). The split is time-based: all training interactions occur before the test window, so future user behavior does not leak into training (page 6).

For comparison, the training set has 209K query-level instances involving 4.4M unique member profiles across queries, candidates, and history users (page 6).

The MAR@k metrics are not scored over these 4-candidate instances. They use a fixed pool of 100 candidates built from logged candidates and sampled negatives (page 7, Section 5.1 and Table 1).
